subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Overrunning Clutches: Freewheeling on Demand
description: A quick win: understand Overrunning Clutches: Freewheeling on Demand.

hook.text: Stop pedaling a bicycle and you coast freely. An overrunning clutch inside the hub lets the wheel outrun the pedals.

buildup.text: Spring-loaded rollers wedge between an inner and outer race in one direction. In the other direction, they slip — freewheeling.

discovery.text: The clutch locks when the inner race drives. When the outer race outruns it, the rollers retract and the link breaks.

twist.text: Starter motors use overrunning clutches. The motor cranks the engine, then the engine outruns the motor and the clutch releases.

climax.text: Conveyor systems, helicopters, and wind turbines all use overrunning clutches to prevent backward drive when the input stops.

punchline.text: Drive forward: locked. Coast ahead: free. One-way torque, automatically.

quiz.question: Why do starter motors need an overrunning clutch?
options: To amplify the torque needed to turn over a cold engine
To disconnect the motor once the engine outruns it after starting — preventing damage
To reduce electrical draw from the battery during cranking
